title: Serengeti National Park: A Complete Guide
excerpt: The Serengeti is Tanzania's most famous park: endless plains, big cats and the Great Migration. Everything you need to know before you go.
body:
The Serengeti covers around 14,750 square kilometres of grassland, woodland and rivers in northern Tanzania. Its name comes from the Maa word for "endless plains". It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the best places in Africa to see wildlife.

## What you can see

- Lions, leopards and cheetahs, often on the same day.
- Elephants, giraffes, buffaloes, zebras and many antelope.
- Hyenas, jackals and with luck a serval or bat-eared fox.
- More than 500 bird species.
- The [Great Migration](/great-wildebeest-migration/) of wildebeest and zebra.

## The regions

The Serengeti is so large that each region has its own character. Central (Seronera), south (Ndutu), west (Grumeti) and north (Mara River). See [the four regions explained](/blog/serengeti-regions-explained/).

## When to go

All year round. The best region depends on the month and where the migration is. See [the migration month by month](/blog/great-migration-month-by-month/).

## How long

At least two nights, preferably three or four. See [how many days in the Serengeti](/blog/serengeti-how-many-days/).

## Getting there

By road from Arusha via Ngorongoro (about eight hours with stops), or by light aircraft to one of the airstrips.

## Where to stay

From simple campsites to tented camps and lodges. See [lodge or tented camp](/blog/lodge-or-tented-camp/).

Read our [Serengeti destination page](/national-parks/serengeti/) or [plan your Serengeti safari](/travel-proposal/).
